packages.label_en: The Divine Portion from Above and the Inner Voice
packages.reason: The entire Torah rests on a single bechina: 'חֶלְקִי יְיָ' (My portion is God, Psalms 119:57) IS 'הַחֵלֶק אֱלֹקַּי מִמַּעַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי' — the divine spark that each person carries from above. The Rebbe reinterprets the verse's 'אָמַרְתִּי' (I said) not as the human speaker declaring his intention, but as the divine portion SPEAKING to the person: it tells him and teaches him 'לִשְׁמֹר דְּבָרֶיךָ' (to keep Your words). This yields two interrelated bechina identities: (1) 'חֶלְקִי יְיָ' IS 'הַחֵלֶק אֱלֹקַּי מִמַּעַל' — the verse-phrase and the interpretive phrase are two names for the same metaphysical reality: the divine portion within the person. (2) 'אָמַרְתִּי' (the saying/teaching) IS attributed to this divine portion — the divine portion shares the nature of an inner teacher who speaks and instructs. These three concepts — the divine portion, the inner voice/saying, and the teaching/instruction — are all aspects of one thematic cluster: the divine inner-teacher who guides the soul toward observance of the commandments. The polarity is entirely positive (good): this is a teaching about the divine light within every person guiding him toward Torah and mitzvot; there is no evil mirror developed in this two-line Torah.

text_extracted_bechinas.explanation: The verse phrase 'חֶלְקִי יְיָ' (My portion is God) IS the 'חֵלֶק אֱלֹקַּי מִמַּעַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי' (the divine portion from above that I have). The Rebbe expands the compressed verse into its full Kabbalistic content: each person possesses a divine portion from above (ref. Job 31:2 — 'וְחֵלֶק אֱלֹהַּ מִמָּעַל'), and this is what 'חֶלְקִי יְיָ' means. The two phrases are different names for the same entity.

text_extracted_bechinas.source_text: אוֹמֵר לִי וּמְלַמֵּד אוֹתִי לִשְׁמֹר דְּבָרֶיךָ
text_extracted_bechinas.explanation: The verse's 'אָמַרְתִּי' (I said) is reattributed by the Rebbe to the subject 'הַחֵלֶק אֱלֹקַּי מִמַּעַל' — making the divine portion the one who SAYS and TEACHES. The divine portion IS the inner voice/teacher (אוֹמֵר לִי וּמְלַמֵּד אוֹתִי). These are not two separate things — the divine spark that each person possesses shares its essential nature with the inner teaching-voice that guides toward mitzvot. The Rebbe collapses the human's 'I said' into 'my divine portion said to me', equating the divine portion with the act/function of spiritual instruction.
